review: The upgraded version seems very unstable but it is still a really fun game. Probably the best simulator ever created for Star Wars.

STAR WARS: X-Wing Alliance is often considered the ultimate evolution of the classic X-Wing space simulator series, combining cinematic storytelling, deep tactical combat, and large-scale space warfare into one of the most immersive Star Wars games ever created. Unlike earlier entries that focused primarily on military campaigns and anonymous pilots, X-Wing Alliance introduces a much more personal narrative centered around the Azzameen family, traders and smugglers whose lives gradually become entangled in the growing conflict between the Rebel Alliance and the Galactic Empire. This stronger emotional focus gives the game a more memorable identity while still preserving the strategic space combat that made the series legendary among PC gamers.

The story follows Ace Azzameen, a young pilot working alongside his family in a dangerous galaxy increasingly dominated by Imperial control and political instability. Early missions focus on cargo transport, escort duties, and commercial rivalries involving the powerful Viraxo corporation, but the narrative slowly escalates into something much larger as the family becomes drawn into Rebel operations during the events surrounding the original Star Wars trilogy. This slower progression works remarkably well because it allows players to connect with the Azzameen family before the larger war begins to consume their lives. Unlike previous games where the player mainly served as a faceless military pilot, Ace feels like a genuine character with personal stakes tied directly to the unfolding conflict.

One of the game’s most impressive qualities is how effectively it captures the atmosphere of the Star Wars universe. The moment players enter the cockpit, the experience immediately feels authentic through detailed ship interiors, mission briefings, radio communication, and dynamic music that recreates the tension of galactic warfare. The game constantly reinforces the illusion that players are actively participating in important events happening alongside the original film trilogy. Massive fleet battles, escort operations, and covert Rebel missions all contribute to the feeling of existing within the larger Star Wars timeline rather than simply observing it from the outside.

The gameplay itself remains incredibly deep and rewarding even years after release. Unlike arcade-style space shooters focused entirely on reflexes, X-Wing Alliance emphasizes tactical combat and resource management. Players must constantly balance shield power, laser energy, engine speed, targeting systems, and situational awareness during intense dogfights. Success depends not only on aiming accuracy but also on understanding how to manage a ship’s systems effectively during battle. This simulation-heavy design creates a much more immersive and strategic experience than many modern Star Wars games.

Mission design is another major strength. The campaign consistently introduces varied objectives that keep gameplay feeling fresh across its long runtime. Players participate in cargo escorts, reconnaissance operations, smuggling runs, rescue missions, fleet assaults, and major battles involving dozens of starfighters and capital ships simultaneously. Many missions evolve dynamically as reinforcements arrive or objectives suddenly change mid-operation, forcing players to react quickly and adapt their strategies. This unpredictability prevents missions from becoming repetitive and helps maintain excitement throughout the campaign.

The variety of playable ships adds tremendous depth to the experience as well. Players are not limited to standard starfighters and eventually gain access to X-Wings, Y-Wings, A-Wings, B-Wings, transports, freighters, and even the Millennium Falcon itself. Each ship handles differently and fulfills unique tactical roles during combat. Fast interceptors prioritize agility, while heavier bombers focus on firepower and durability. The inclusion of multi-crew ships was especially impressive because players could switch between piloting and turret control during missions, creating larger and more cinematic battle scenarios.

Visually, the game represented a major technical leap for the series during its original release period. Fully rendered 3D cockpits, improved lighting effects, larger battle environments, and more detailed ship models helped create a far more cinematic presentation than earlier entries. Even today, massive engagements involving Star Destroyers, Mon Calamari cruisers, and swarms of starfighters still manage to feel epic because of the game’s strong sense of scale and atmosphere.

The sound design also deserves enormous praise. Familiar Star Wars music dynamically shifts during missions and battles, reinforcing dramatic moments while helping create the feeling of participating in an actual Star Wars film. Radio chatter between pilots and commanders keeps battles feeling alive, while the fully voiced cutscenes and briefings strengthen the cinematic storytelling significantly. Few Star Wars games manage to capture the audio atmosphere of the films this effectively.

Another area where X-Wing Alliance excels is its integration into the larger Star Wars timeline. The campaign overlaps with important events from the original trilogy and even includes connections to Shadows of the Empire. Players eventually participate in operations tied directly to the Battle of Endor, giving the later missions a genuine sense of historical importance within the Star Wars universe. These connections make the campaign feel meaningful rather than isolated from the broader lore.

However, modern players may struggle with the game’s age in several areas. The controls are extremely complicated compared to contemporary flight games, relying heavily on keyboard shortcuts and detailed system management. New players unfamiliar with classic space simulators may initially find the learning curve intimidating. The game expects patience and practice before its mechanics fully become comfortable.

The visuals, while groundbreaking during the late 1990s, are obviously outdated by current standards. Ship models and textures appear simplistic today, and some interface elements feel clunky compared to modern design conventions. Despite this, the strong art direction and atmosphere still help preserve much of the game’s cinematic appeal.

Difficulty can also become unforgiving during later missions. Certain operations require near-perfect execution, especially during large fleet battles involving multiple objectives and enemy squadrons simultaneously. Players who fail to manage shields or energy systems properly can be destroyed quickly. The steep challenge level may frustrate casual players, but it also creates a satisfying sense of accomplishment for those willing to master the game’s systems.

Despite these aging elements, STAR WARS: X-Wing Alliance remains one of the most ambitious and immersive Star Wars games ever made. Its combination of emotional storytelling, strategic gameplay, cinematic presentation, and large-scale space combat helped define the space simulation genre for years afterward. Even decades later, few games have recreated the fantasy of participating in Rebel starfighter operations during the Galactic Civil War with this much authenticity and depth.

For fans of Star Wars, tactical space combat, and classic PC simulators, X-Wing Alliance remains an essential experience. While the dated visuals and demanding controls may require patience from modern audiences, the outstanding atmosphere, memorable campaign, and deep combat mechanics continue to make it one of the greatest Star Wars games ever created.

Rating: 8/10

[h1] Космосим по ЗВ не только с тактикой, но и с сюжетом [/h1]

 Это пиковая ступень развития тактикульных космосимов от "Лукасов". Всё, что мы видели в предыдущих частях развито, расширено и отполировано, если в двух словах мы - полноценный пилот космического корабля, перед которым, помимо управления кораблём ещё и стоят сюжетные задачи. Сюжет неплохой, история начинается с космической торговли и постепенно закручивается до участия в извечной борьбе "хороших" и "плохих". И если без спойлеров, он затягивает, почти как фильм, тем более, что есть куча отсылок к ранним эпизодам ЗВ.
 Графика очень порадовала. Здесь она на голову выше, чем в x-wing vs tie fighter, очень чёткие и прорисованные текстуры, для тех лет, чистое не мыльное изображение и космическое пространство теперь не выглядит, как унылый плоский задник, нарисованный на картонке. А ещё, легким движением руки здесь (впервые!) можно вертеть головой в кабине, почти как в war thunder, ну круто же!
 Помимо этого здесь никуда не делось управление двигателями, щитами, перераспределением энергии, появилась возможность стыковки (!) с кораблями, пишу и даже не верится, что это про игру "нулевых". Кроме того, идут постоянные фоновые радиопереговоры, что добавляет атмосферы, а не как раньше, только на на наши действия кто-то там что-то бубнил в эфир.

[h2] Плюсы [/h2]

- Сюжет. Не хватаёт звезд с неба, однако не вторичен и в какой-то момент герою даже сопереживаешь
- Объем. В этой части космос выглядит действительно масшатбным. В некоторых сражениях можно увидеть просто рой различных кораблей, что добавляет к погружению

- Локализация. Тоже отнесу это к минусам, хотя лично для меня, после 5 игр, без локализации, это уже не представляет серьезных проблем

[b] По итогу игру могу порекомендовать ценителям. Нужно понимать, что это достаточно нишевой продукт, хоть в этот раз они и попытались приблизиться к массе казуалов, запилив неплохой сюжет. Если отсутствие локализации и куча кнопок Вас не пугает, то эта игра точно для Вас [/b]

[h2]Resumen del Juego[/h2]
STAR WARS™ - X-Wing Alliance™ es acción espacial pura: te subes a una nave, te tiran al vacío y tu trabajo es convertir el espacio en un tráfico infernal de láseres, misiles y decisiones de “¿por qué me metí aquí?”. No es un paseo cinemático moderno: es un simulador espacial con alma de escuela vieja donde volar bien importa más que posar para la cámara.

La propuesta es sencilla y adictiva: campañas de combate con enfoque de piloto, misiones con objetivos claros (y a veces crueles) y un ritmo de acción que te exige atención constante. La primera impresión es clara: esto no intenta ser “amigable”, intenta ser “Star Wars en la cabina”, con todo lo que eso implica… incluyendo el cariño por el sufrimiento.

Y sí, también tiene multijugador/JcJ, Remote Play Together y Steam Cloud… lo cual suena increíble hasta que miras los jugadores actuales y te das cuenta de que el multijugador hoy es más una reliquia arqueológica que una comunidad viva.

✅ 🚀 Acción en el espacio con sabor clásico: volar y pelear se siente como “simulador espacial”, no como paseo en rieles.  
✅ 🕹️ Un jugador sólido: la experiencia principal no depende de que haya gente conectada.  
✅ ☁️ Steam Cloud: tus avances no se pierden en un agujero negro (bien ahí).

Lo No Tan Bueno:
❌ 👥 Jugadores actuales: 3. El multijugador se siente como organizar una fiesta y que lleguen dos personas… y una es tu primo.  
❌ 🏆 0 logros: Steam te mira y te dice “felicidades por jugar… supongo”.  
❌ 🎮 Compatibilidad parcial con mando: o sea, “sí… pero no llores si algo se siente tosco”.

This classic STAR WARS game let's you fly iconic and lesser known ships from the STAR WARS universe. Back when it was released this game brought so much innovation to the genre of sci-fi flight sims, and apart from the obviously outdated graphics, the game still holds his own among the older games out there.

LucasArts launched its last real space combat shooter on the market in 1999. In X-Wing: Alliance, we take on the role of civilian pilot ‘Ace’ Azameen, the youngest member of an old transport dynasty of the same name. Set between Episodes V and VI, the family, which initially wants to pursue its business neutrally, must increasingly assert itself in a galaxy-wide conflict between the Rebel Alliance and the Empire as well as unscrupulous competitors. However, the Azameens, who have been in business for centuries, are not so easily intimidated. After all, the family's reputation as a reliable transport company is at stake. But when the Galactic Civil War inevitably threatens to disrupt the business, the Azameens forge a risky plan. They go on the offensive. And strike back...

What is impressive about the game still today is not only the freedom of play, but also the high level of detail for its time and the excellent story structure. Instead of predictable plot twists or ridiculous mind-changes of protagonists (Yes, EA´s Squadrons...), fans are rewarded with an ingeniously thought-out background story that, like the other projects of its time, fits seamlessly into the storyline of the old Legacy trilogy. The fact that we have to help the smuggler Dash Rendar hijack an Imperial secret freighter and even steal the shuttle "Tyderium" in another mission was worthy of a film itself and proved how great the writers combined background events from even different video games without seeming desperately or ridiculous. It added depth to the game world and gave new significant weight to the events between Episode V and VI.

It also offered a full voiceover soundtrack and full in-flight dialogue, which made the dogfights way more dynamic. Flight controls were marginally updated from the previous games of the series, but even allowed to link different energy weapons to fire together, as well as managing your onboard energy supply. Another aspect is that the game is quite challenging right from the start and at times frustratingly difficult, even on medium level. It can also only be played with a joystick in combination with your keyboard. And keep in Mind that the game does not take the player ‘by the hand’ - right from the start, you are thrown into the icy expanses of space and entrusted with quite challenging missions. However, this aspect alone gives the game its appeal.

It´s also recommended to pay close attention to the briefings before the flight - because there are many pitfalls that can cause an entire mission to fail. But those pilots who bring time, skill and a love of learning as well as a good dose of frustration tolerance will be rewarded with an excellent adventure in a galaxy far, far away. And anyone who has completed the journey should definitely try out the game with the ingenious mods that are available online. "X-Wing Alliance Upgrade" and "TIE Fighter Total Conversion" deserves praise here. One can only hope that such games will retain their fanbase, so that a new generation of fans will learn to appreciate and preserve the old classic Legacy Timeline of Star Wars for the future. So, fasten your seatbelts and prepare to jump into Lightspeed!

I have fond memories of X-Wing Versus TIE Fighter, which is considered the worst of the X-Wing series for its lack of narrative and focus on multiplayer in comparison to its predecessors, but it is still my favorite of the series. I received Star Wars: Squadrons from Epic Games for free, and after a week, I decided to check up on the X-Wing Alliance Upgrade mods and found the TIE Fighter Total Conversion mod, and I have been smiling the night I successfully installed them! There is just something charming about old games, especially when the developers realize graphics of the age were not enough to bring in players. It is in my opinion that vanilla X-Wing Alliance is superior to Squadrons, and with the XWAU mod, there is little question for me!

If you have gotten Squadrons for free, it is playable, but the gameplay mechanics is a simplified version of the X-wing formula making it approachable by players new to flight sims. If you have to buy one or the other, Squadrons has better graphics, aesthetic customization, and quick 5v5 ranked gameplay if you want to seek to top scoreboards. X-Wing Alliance is a classic, beloved by many LucasArts fans, with controls that might be initially overwhelming to newer players, but requires more skill and offers a compelling story, but innately requires a joystick or controller. Both include training missions so you can get acclimated with the controls. With the inclusion of XWAU, you gain updated graphics and have the option to use alternative controls if you do not have a joystick. Add the TFTC mod, you now have two games in one, albeit with the complexities of modding.

The price of Squadrons on Steam is $40USD. X-Wing Alliance is $10USD. If you can get it for free, play Squadrons. If you have to pay for one or the other, even if they are the same price, buy X-Wing Alliance.

You can find the mods at https://www.xwaupgrade.com/
